title: The Semantic Source Store write authority is method-granular
summary: SemanticSourceRepositoryService (oorexx_semantic_source_store, 2026-10-23) is the authority that turns imports into semantic source objects and revisions. Before it, nothing in the estate wrote ssc_source_object or ssc_source_revision; every reader read empty tables. Each structural object (METHOD, ATTRIBUTE, CONSTANT, ROUTINE, REQUIRES, OPTIONS, CLASS header, EXECUTABLE_SECTION, unknown directive fragment) is its own object with its own revision chain. Each file is a SOURCE_UNIT object whose revision text is the ordered member list. Acceptance is explicit and authorized.
invariants: Granularity is the method: a changed method body is one new revision of one object; classes are never imported as single blobs.
Identity is language + module + logical path + semantic key; a version-wrapped archive folder (pkg_v0.1-dev24/) is packaging, not identity.
A SOURCE_UNIT layout revision changes only when members are added, removed or reordered.
New revisions are PROPOSED; only acceptRevision/acceptImport with an authenticated principal and a passing authorizer make them served. No authorizer means DENIED.
Every import records an immutable per-import projection (project_id import:<id>); the exact imported bytes stay reproducible after later acceptances.
Every new revision is read back and SHA-256 compared before the member is marked IMPORTED; a backend that alters bytes is refused (STORAGE_NOT_LOSSLESS), never trusted.
All ids are content-derived and the member row is written last, so repeated or interrupted imports are safe to re-run (ALREADY_IMPORTED).

Read files through SemanticSourceLayoutPackageService, not SemanticSourcePackageService: the parent's getPackage crashes on a real database (RESULT variable overwritten by a bare ~append instruction) and assembles files in unordered .Directory order.
